V1.verbatim: In the Wikimedia platform, the impact of many new features are tested using controlled experiments.
The most common way to bucket editors for A/B tests has been on their user ID.

The Wikimedia Foundation has been testing new ways of making human knowledge even more accessible. Known as experiments, these short, time-bound projects help us better understand how Wikipedia can reach new audiences, respond to global trends, and meet the evolving needs of internet users.

V2.onde: Seção "How We Use Information We Receive From You" > "General"
V2.verbatim: We and our service providers use your information for the legitimate purpose of pursuing our charitable mission, including:

We use this information to make your experience with the Wikimedia Sites safer and better, to gain a greater understanding of user preferences and their interaction with the Wikimedia Sites, and to generally improve our services.
Similarly, we share non-Personal Information or aggregated information with researchers, scholars, academics, and other interested third parties who wish to study the Wikimedia Sites.

V2.onde: Resumo ("Be aware") no topo da Privacy Policy
V2.verbatim: As part of our commitment to education and research around the world, we occasionally release public information and aggregated or non-personal information to the general public through data dumps and data sets.
We cannot work collectively without gathering, sharing, and analyzing information about our users as we seek new ways to make the Wikimedia Sites more usable, safer, and more beneficial.
This generally applies for any study that might affect our users. An experiment, a survey, or a large-scale interview study, etc.
